chapter: New Orleans musicians, recordings and radio
title: Broadcasting from London to New York and her own radio show, 1937
summary: Fred Bate heard her in Paris; after a London-to-New York broadcast she got a 20-week WEAF/WJZ contract and her own show with Norman Cloutier's band, then the Basin Street society and WOR.

venues.name: Chamber Music Society of Lower Basin Street

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Let's get back to the '30's now. You -- were you featured on -- you were featured on an NBC radio series.
Oh, yes. See? After I came back from Showboat, I -- well, while I was in London, Mr. -- when I was

in Paris, just before -- I had gone from Showboat over to Paris again for a little while, and I was singing in Fred Payne's bar, and Edward G. Robinson brought Mr. Bate, Fred Bate in, and Mr. Bate heard me sing, and he told me anytime I was ready to come back to New York to just let him know.

Well, I thought it was a little talk, you know, and you know how you think people promise you things. So then I went back to London, and while I was at the Palladium -- I believe I was at the Palladium -- Mr. -- I was either at the Palladium or I -- or either singing with Jack Jackson at the Dorchester, but I think I was at the Palladium, because I -- they arranged a date for me to record -- I mean to broadcast from London to New York, and Leslie Hutchinson played for me.

And I think that was for the New York office to hear me, to see if they really wanted me, you see? And I broadcast from London to New York, and I immediately got notice to come on to New York. They sent me a contract for 20 weeks for NBC -- not NBC. It was the WEAF and WJZ -- to broadcast with them. See?

And I came right on back -- on my way on the ocean, I received a wire from Mr. John Royal saying that, as I -- as the boat landed, to come right up to his office, and I went right to his office in Rockefeller, you know, Center, and they gave me, as I said, my contract.
And I opened -- I mean I had my own show with Norman

Clothier -- big white band -- I think it was 25 pieces -- with Henry Levine. And what's the fellow now that has the big orchestra, one of them known for classics. It'll come to me. Anyhow, I had my own show with Norman Clothier's band, and, oh, if I could think of that fellow's name because he's so popular now with his big classical band.
Big classical band? Not Arthur Fiedler.

No. It'll come to me before we get through, I think. But now, when I would be -- when I'd sing my jazz part, Norman Clothier and his group would play on this side, and they had a mike set up right, just run right on to the next mike, and Levine would play the sweet stuff for me. See? That's how they arranged it.
What was the show called?
Alberta Hunter.
Alberta Hunter Show?
That's right. And then from there --
And that was when? The early '30's or when?
1937. That was 1937, because I remember that so well.
Did you have a sponsor?
No, just what -- just tell you the man who heard me, you know, in Paris, and had me broadcast from London to
America.
I mean you didn't have a commercial sponsor?
No, uh-uh. No, I know what you mean. I didn't have a sponsor. And then from that I sang with -- I had the Basin Street Society --
Oh, the Chamber music society of Lower Basin Street? (inaudible)?
Lower Basin Street, that's right.
Henry Levine and then when I --
when I -- I think I had an engagement to go someplace else anyhow. Dinah Shore followed me in.
And Lena Horne.
I don't know about Lena. Was it? Well, I know Dinah Shore followed me in. And then when I finished that, then I -- WOR -- went to WOR, and I had quite a long stay with WOR.
Your own show again?
Yeah. Each time, my own. And then every time I'd always get contracts to come back to Europe, and I'd go back and forth to Europe all the time, you see.
